subject: computer-science
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In functional programming, the higher-order function 'map' does what?
options: Selects only elements that satisfy a predicate
Applies a given function to every element of a list, returning a new list
Sorts a list into ascending order
Reduces a list to a single accumulated value
questions.explain: map applies a function to each element of a list and returns a new list of the transformed results.

questions.q: Which higher-order function returns only the elements of a list that satisfy a given predicate?
questions.explain: filter tests each element against a predicate and keeps only those for which it returns true.

questions.q: Which bus carries signals such as 'memory read', 'memory write' and clock pulses?
questions.explain: The control bus carries control signals that coordinate and synchronise the activities of the system.

questions.q: A class can be described as:
options: A template or blueprint defining the attributes and methods of objects
A specific instance occupying memory at run time
questions.explain: A class is a template specifying the attributes and methods that its objects (instances) will have.

questions.q: Which programming paradigm is characterised by writing programs as a sequence of statements that change program state, using procedures/subroutines?
questions.explain: Procedural programming structures code as ordered statements grouped into procedures that operate on shared mutable state.

questions.q: A record (struct) data type is best described as:
options: A collection of related fields that may be of different data types
A collection of elements of the same type accessed by index
questions.explain: A record groups together several named fields that can hold different data types.

questions.q: How does segmentation differ from paging?
options: Segments are fixed-size; pages are variable
Segmentation cannot be used with virtual memory
Segmentation removes the need for an address bus
Segments are variable-sized logical divisions; pages are fixed-size
questions.explain: Segmentation divides memory into variable-sized logical units, whereas paging uses fixed-size blocks.

questions.q: Which development methodology emphasises iterative delivery, frequent customer feedback and adapting to changing requirements?
questions.explain: Agile delivers software in short iterations, embracing changing requirements and continuous customer collaboration.

questions.q: The Rapid Application Development (RAD) approach is characterised by:
options: Building prototypes quickly with heavy user involvement and iterative refinement
A single long development phase with no user input
Releasing only after exhaustive up-front documentation
questions.explain: RAD relies on rapid prototyping and close user feedback to refine the system iteratively.

questions.q: In OOP, abstraction is best described as:
options: Representing essential features while hiding unnecessary implementation detail
Copying one object's data into another
Passing an address to a subroutine
Allowing a method to take many forms
questions.explain: Abstraction models only the relevant, essential characteristics of something, suppressing irrelevant detail.

questions.q: A subclass acquiring the attributes and methods of a superclass is an example of which OOP concept?
questions.explain: Inheritance lets a subclass derive and reuse the attributes and methods defined in its superclass.

questions.q: In object-oriented programming, what does encapsulation primarily achieve?
options: Allowing one method name to behave differently for different object types
Bundling data and the methods that act on it, hiding internal state behind an interface
Allowing a subclass to acquire attributes and methods of a superclass
Creating multiple instances from one class definition
questions.explain: Encapsulation binds attributes and methods together within a class and restricts direct external access to the internal data.

questions.q: What essential feature must every recursive routine include to avoid infinite recursion?
questions.explain: A base case provides a condition under which the recursion stops rather than calling itself again.

questions.q: In functional programming, 'immutability' means that:
options: Functions cannot be passed as arguments
Once created, data values cannot be changed
questions.explain: Immutability means data cannot be altered after creation; transformations produce new values instead.

questions.q: On a UML class diagram, an arrow with a hollow triangular head pointing from a subclass to a superclass represents:
questions.explain: A hollow triangle pointing to the parent class denotes a generalisation/inheritance relationship.

questions.q: Which of these is an advantage of object-oriented programming over purely procedural programming?
options: It removes the need for variables
Encapsulation and inheritance promote code reuse and easier maintenance
questions.explain: OOP supports modularity, reuse through inheritance, and maintainability via encapsulation of state and behaviour.

questions.q: Exception handling using a try/catch (try/except) structure is primarily used to:
options: Detect and respond to runtime errors without crashing the program
questions.explain: Try/catch blocks let a program catch runtime errors and handle them gracefully instead of terminating abnormally.

questions.q: Black-box testing is best described as testing that:
options: Measures the speed of the program
Checks every internal branch and loop of the code
Is performed only by end users after release
Tests functionality against the specification without knowledge of the internal code
questions.explain: Black-box testing validates inputs and expected outputs against the spec, treating the implementation as opaque.

questions.q: In the software development life cycle, which model proceeds through fixed sequential stages with little overlap or return to earlier phases?
questions.explain: The waterfall model moves linearly through distinct phases, each completed before the next begins.

questions.q: What does polymorphism mean in object-oriented programming?
options: Defining a class as a template for objects
Restricting access to an object's internal data
Hiding implementation detail from the user
The ability for the same method call to take many forms depending on the object's type
questions.explain: Polymorphism literally means 'many forms', allowing a single interface or method name to behave differently across object types.

questions.q: When a parameter is passed by reference rather than by value, what is actually passed to the subroutine?
options: The memory address of the variable
questions.explain: Passing by reference passes the address of the variable, so changes inside the subroutine affect the original.

questions.q: Which of these is a defining feature of pure functional programming?
options: Sequential modification of state through loops
Immutability and functions treated as first-class objects
Heavy use of global mutable variables
Functions with side effects on shared state
questions.explain: Functional programming emphasises immutable data and first-class functions that can be passed and returned like any value.

questions.q: What is meant by describing functions as 'first-class objects' in a language?
options: They can be assigned to variables, passed as arguments and returned from other functions
They execute faster than other code
They can only be called from the main program
They must always return an integer
questions.explain: First-class functions can be stored, passed as parameters, and returned just like any other value.

questions.q: Which statement about passing a parameter by value is correct?
options: A copy of the data is made, so changes inside the subroutine do not affect the original
Only arrays may be passed this way
The variable's address is shared with the subroutine
The subroutine can permanently alter the caller's original variable
questions.explain: By value passes a copy, so modifications within the subroutine leave the caller's original variable unchanged.

questions.q: Which testing method examines internal code structure and logic paths rather than just inputs and outputs?
questions.explain: White-box testing inspects the internal logic and code paths, whereas black-box testing ignores the implementation.

questions.q: Which paradigm expresses logic as facts and rules, with the system inferring answers to queries (e.g. Prolog)?
questions.explain: Logic (declarative) programming states facts and rules and lets an inference engine derive results from queries.

questions.q: Selection in programming is implemented by which type of construct?
questions.explain: Selection chooses between paths of execution using conditional constructs such as IF or CASE.

questions.q: Which of the following is a key benefit of using an Integrated Development Environment (IDE)?
options: It compiles code without any errors ever occurring
It removes the need for any testing
It combines an editor, debugger and tools such as autocompletion in one application
It guarantees the program is logically correct
questions.explain: An IDE integrates editing, debugging, syntax highlighting and other development aids in a single environment.

questions.q: The 'reduce' (fold) higher-order function is used to:
options: Reverse the order of a list
Return a new list of the same length
Combine the elements of a list into a single accumulated value
questions.explain: reduce repeatedly applies a combining function to accumulate the list's elements into one result value.

questions.q: A variable declared inside a subroutine that is only accessible within that subroutine has which scope?
questions.explain: A local variable exists only within the subroutine in which it is declared and cannot be accessed outside it.
